Long-term memory supports agents across ses-
sions. Repeated retrieval and write-back can let
one historical claim occupy multiple retrieval
positions and influence current answers with-
out independent evidence. Existing work exam-
ines retrieval, updating, and question answer-
ing, leaving same-source record accumulation
and post-correction persistence underexplored.
Motivated by research in social cognition and
memory psychology on repeated exposure, re-
trieval, and revision, we defineMemory Echoas
the excess retrieval exposure gained by histori-
cal information from the same source without
additional independent evidence, and introduce
MEchoBench to evaluate its emergence, cor-
rection resistance, persistence, and effect on
answers. To address this phenomenon, we intro-
duce the Family–Provenance–Authority frame-
work (FPA). Specifically, FPA selects one rep-
resentative per source

• We develop MEchoBench and four measure-
ments to track trace accumulation, correction
resistance, delayed persistence, and answer
shift within one memory lifecycle.
• We introduce FPA, combining family repre-
sentative selection, post-correction eligibility,
and authority-guided answering to reduce de-
cision contamination while preserving trace-
able history, and validate its effects across
general data sources and practical tasks.

Stage 2: Provenance-aware gating.The gate
checks source, parent, verification, and validity
against the correction. In the figure, M4 supersedes
the whole-milk family: M1–M3 remain stored
for audit but cannot support the current answer.
M4 enters as verified evidence; nonconflicting M5
and M6 remain eligible context. Retrieval nei-
ther grants a record write-back authority nor re-
stores an obsolete descendant's evidential status.

et al., 2026b), and LangMem (LangChain Team,

questions in four architectures yield 1,520 paired

5.6 (gpt-5.6-sol) judges answers in two passes.

histories, and candidate pools. ED and WEP de-
pend on the served pool, so they match across gen-
erators. We compare methods within each model;

evidence.excerpt:
The ablation separates suppressing obsolete evi-
dence from supplying a usable answer. Provenance
control alone sharply reduces old-answer adoption
but does not improve correctness; family control by
itself can also remove useful context. Combining
the two gates further reduces the historical claim's
reach but leaves the generator short of a replace-
ment answer. Accuracy recovers when verified au-
thority is added, and the answer check contributes a
smaller final gain (Table 3). Together, these stages
limit unsupported repetition and supply the current
fact.

The benchmark places a real answer from another
question into a controlled historical position; it
does not estimate how frequently such seeds arise
in natural interaction. Serving-method compar-
isons replay recorded candidate pools rather than
evolving a separate memory database for each com-
parator. FPA uses source-family and validity anno-
tations supplied by the benchmark, and its final an-
swer check can select a concise verified span, mak-
ing part of the measured gain an answer-processing
effect. GPT-5.6 judges correctness and contamina-
tion without an independent human audit of bor-
derline cases. The travel and missing-correction
conditions show that the measured benefit depends
on a relevant Echo conflict and usable replacement
evidence.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The accuracy and DCE gains are corroborated by deterministic rank/trace-based exposure metrics and by consistent paired results across two generators, DeepSeek V4 Flash and Kimi K2.6.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by GPT-5.6 judge-assigned correctness and contamination scores, alongside deterministic retrieval-occupancy metrics (ED, RRI, WEP) computed from the served candidate pool.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The FPA serving pipeline is shaped by fixed rule-based scoring formulas, benchmark-supplied source-family and validity annotations, and a final answer check that can select a concise verified span.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims closely match the empirical data, and the authors explicitly document failure cases and scope boundaries, such as performance drops when reliable replacement evidence is absent or in non-conflicting domains like travel planning.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation is rigorous, covering 190 questions across four memory frameworks (A-MEM, Mem0, CoM, LangMem) and two LLM generators (DeepSeek V4 Flash and Kimi K2.6) with paired controls, strong baselines (CRAG-M, PairLR, Budget), sequential ablations, and bootstrap intervals.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline accuracy and contamination trends are confirmed by deterministic rank/trace-based metrics (Echo Density, WEP) and dual-model evaluations (DeepSeek V4 Flash and Kimi K2.6).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Evaluation relies on multi-pass grading by an independent LLM judge (GPT-5.6) alongside deterministic retrieval occupancy metrics (ED, RRI, WEP).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Rule-based scoring formulas and benchmark-supplied provenance annotations determine candidate selection, gating, and answer constraints.

primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge key limitations, including the reliance on benchmark-provided source annotations, synthetic seeds placed into historical traces, answer span selection influencing gains, and lack of human audit for borderline judge scores.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing five lifecycle evaluation stages, well-defined mathematical metrics (ED, RRI, WEP, DCE), and a modular three-stage serving framework (FPA) that regulates memory contexts without mutating historical storage.
primary.quality_rationale: This study makes a well-controlled, significant contribution to understanding and mitigating failure modes in agent memory architectures. The experimental design is meticulous with sound comparative baselines and well-scoped claims.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper formalizes 'Memory Echo' in LLM agent long-term memory architectures, introduces MEchoBench to measure trace accumulation and persistence across five lifecycle stages, and proposes the Family-Provenance-Authority (FPA) serving framework to mitigate decision contamination.

scholarly_quality.rationale: This study makes a well-controlled, significant contribution to understanding and mitigating failure modes in agent memory architectures. The experimental design is meticulous with sound comparative baselines and well-scoped claims.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors acknowledge key limitations, including the reliance on benchmark-provided source annotations, synthetic seeds placed into historical traces, answer span selection influencing gains, and lack of human audit for borderline judge scores.
